assays.assay_description: Mice with implanted head-mounted neodymium magnets placed in a 12.5-cm glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil; head twitches detected via waveform analysis or AI for 20-40 min sessions. Tested across many compounds, doses, antagonist pretreatments (M100907, pimavanserin, YM-254890 ICV, edelfosine), and repeated-dose tolerance regimens.

application_type.evidence: 25N derivatives... were injected SC... pimavanserin, edelfosine, R-(-)-DOI, (±)-DOI... were injected IP; YM-254,890 was injected into the lateral ventricle (2 µL)

setup_habituation.evidence: HTR experiments were conducted in a well-lit room, and the mice were allowed to habituate to the room for at least 1 h prior to testing (room habituation only, no apparatus pre-exposure described)

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were tested in a 12.5-cm diameter glass cylinder surrounded by a magnetometer coil

outcomes.summary: Classical psychedelics (DOI, LSD, psilocin, 5-MeO-DMT, DET, 25N-NBOMe, 25O-NBOMe, 2C2-NBOMe, 25O-NBcP) dose-dependently induced head twitches, whereas β-arrestin-biased 5-HT2A agonists (25N-N1-Nap, 25N-NBPh, 25N-NB-2-OH-3-Me, 25O-N1-Nap, 2C2-N1-Nap) and low-Gq-efficacy compounds (lisuride, 2-Br-LSD, 6-F-DET, 6-MeO-DMT) failed to induce HTR but blocked DOI-induced HTR. Inhibition of Gq (YM-254890 ICV) or PLC (edelfosine) blocked HTR. Repeated DOI or 25N-N1-Nap produced tolerance; pimavanserin did not. HTR magnitude correlated with 5-HT2A-Gq efficacy.
outcomes.evidence: 25N-NBOMe (4) induces the head-twitch response (HTR)... 25N-N1-Nap (16) does not induce the HTR... Pretreatment with 25N-N1-Nap (16) blocks the HTR induced by (±)-DOI... Repeated administration of (±)-DOI and 25N-N1-Nap (16), but not pimavanserin, induces a tolerance to the HTR induced by DOI

outcomes.summary: 25N-N1-Nap (β-arrestin-biased 5-HT2A agonist) and M100907 (5-HT2A antagonist) both attenuated PCP-induced hyperlocomotion, while having no effect on baseline activity, supporting an antipsychotic-like profile.
outcomes.evidence: 25N-N1-Nap (16) attenuates phencyclidine (PCP)-induced hyperactivity (pretreatment × PCP: F1,20=7.09, p=0.015; pretreatment × PCP × time: F2,40=11.03, p=0.0002)

judge_notes: Two behavioural assays retained: HTR (collapsing all drug, dose, antagonist, ICV-infusion, edelfosine, and repeated/tolerance variants into one assay per rubric) and BPM locomotor activity (PCP hyperactivity blockade).
Dropped all in vitro/structural work (BRET, calcium flux, NanoBit internalization, docking, MD) per rubric exclusions.

B1 set to 0 (1 measure) for both assays: HTR reports counts only; BPM analyzed in main results reports only distance traveled (rearing/holepoking apparatus exists but no separate result variable analyzed).
HTR D1 scored 1 (multiple sessions) because the tolerance experiment includes daily-dosing context with a 24-h follow-up DOI challenge HTR recording; D5 = Yes for the same reason.
C2 setup_habituation marked 'no' for both assays: only room habituation is described, which per rubric does not count as setup_habituation.

Candidates disagreed on B7 classification — paper explicitly uses 'artificial intelligence' to classify head twitches from magnetometer waveforms; this is waveform/signal classification, not video-based pose/behavioural classification, so B7 = 0 retained.
DOI dosing entry consolidated to 'multiple' route and 'repeated' schedule to capture both acute IP challenge and 5-day SC tolerance regimen.
